answer: To resist Sybils, agents cross-audit identity clusters across topological cut boundaries. An adversary fabricating identities on a network knoll must stake capital across every bridge; if multi-agent auditing exposes coordinated voting along a cluster ridge, their staked collateral is slashed. Because each added fake edge triggers auditing over an expanding cut, the attacker faces superlinear attacker cost while legitimate interactions pass smoothly like a zephyr.
